name: Skater Squat / Drop Knee Single-Leg Squat
description: The skater squat is a single-leg squat variation where the rear leg drops straight down toward the floor, with the knee approaching but not fully resting on the ground. Unlike the Bulgarian split squat, the rear foot is free and not elevated, requiring greater balance and demanding very high quadriceps and glute force from the working leg. It is significantly more challenging than a standard split squat.

execution.starting_position: Stand on one foot. Extend the arms forward or hold a small counterbalance weight. The rear leg hangs free behind you.
execution.setup_instructions: Master the bodyweight version before adding load. Practice near a wall for balance assistance initially.
steps: Step 1: Shift weight entirely to the working leg, brace the core.
Step 2: Lower the rear knee straight down toward the floor as you squat down on the working leg.
Step 3: Descend until the rear knee nearly touches the floor while the front shin remains relatively vertical.
Step 4: Drive through the working heel to return to the starting position.
execution.breathing_instructions: Inhale on the descent, exhale on the drive up.
common_mistakes: Rear knee tapping the floor and using it as a support
Excessive forward lean of the torso
safety_considerations: Very high demand on knee and ankle stability — progress very gradually
Use bodyweight for many sessions before adding load
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Rear knee should approach but not touch the floor. Front shin relatively vertical.
coaching_cues: Stand tall on the working leg
Knee traces over the second toe
